description: AS568 dash -010 O-ring: ID 6.07 ± 0.13 mm (0.239 ± 0.005 in) x CS 1.78 ± 0.08 mm (0.070 ± 0.003 in), OD 9.63 mm reference (nominal 1/4 x 3/8 x 1/16 in). Silicone (VMQ) 70 ± 5 Shore A, FDA compliant to 21 CFR 177.2600, -59 to 204 °C in dry air and below 100 °C in hot water; for static seals only. In the smart bottle it is the rod seal on the Ø6 mm probe tube in the cap's probe boss.

material.assumption: The CAD body is the nominal free-state torus (61.37 mm³), so the computed mass is ≈ 0.085 g; Parker's basic volume for -010 is .0037 cu in (60.6 mm³). Specific gravity 1.38 is the supplier's compound test value (ASTM D297), not a lot specification; another supplier's compound (Marco S1000) states none.
material.name: Silicone rubber (VMQ), 70 Shore A, FDA 21 CFR 177.2600 grade (TORS VMQ-70)

metadata.colour: brick red (product page); 'not specified' on the compound sheet
metadata.compound: TORS VMQ-70 (legacy S70), silicone VMQ, compression or transfer moulded
metadata.standard: SAE AS568 (read through Parker ORD 5700A and Apple Rubber; the standard itself was not read)

metadata.operating_note: Product page: heat resistance up to approximately 400 °F (204 °C), cold flexibility down to approximately -75 °F (-59 °C). Compound sheet: -62 to +204 °C continuous in dry air, below +100 °C continuously in hot water; brittleness test passed at -55 °C.

params.description: Parker 2-010 (AS 568A -010): nominal 1/4 ID x 3/8 OD x 1/16 W (in); actual ID .239 ± .005, W .070 ± .003 (in); metric ID 6,07 ± 0,13, W 1,78 ± 0,08 (mm). Apple Rubber: 'O-Rings are specified by I.D. and cross section.'

params.note: Static seal only: the compound has poor abrasion, cut and tear resistance and must not be used in a moving gland. Keep installation stretch under 5 %. Deburr the gland and chamfer every lead-in; do not drag the ring over a sharp edge, burr or thread. Never use silicone grease as the installation lubricant (it swells this compound); use a compatible FDA-grade lubricant. (Parker's Super-O-Lube, a silicone oil, is listed as usable on silicones with 'special consideration'; the compound supplier's instruction is the stricter and is followed.)

interfaces.name: Outside diameter Ø9.63 and flanks (gland seat)

params.description: OD .379 in (9.63 mm), reference only (Parker 'Mean OD (Ref)', Apple Rubber 'Outside diameter (O.D.) is for reference only'). The OD seats on the bottom of a female (bore) gland; the flanks touch the groove side walls, or the two faces in a face seal.

params.note: Parker Design Chart 4-1 (industrial static glands, sizes 004-050, CS .070 in): gland depth L .050-.052 in (1.27-1.32 mm), squeeze 22-32 %, diametral clearance .002-.005 in, halved for silicone, groove width .093-.098 in (2.36-2.49 mm) with no back-up ring, groove radius .005-.015 in. Parker Design Table 4-1, -010: female gland for a tube OD .250 in (6.35 mm) with groove Ø .350 in (8.89 mm) and throat Ø .252 in; male gland bore Ø .375 in with groove Ø .275 in. Apple Rubber (static, CS .070): radial gland depth .050-.055 in, squeeze 18-32 %, groove width .105 in. Compound supplier: static squeeze 15-30 % (toward the high end), gland fill 65-85 % at temperature, static surface finish 16-32 µin Ra.

Derived from the sourced gland rules for the Ø6.0 mm probe tube (adafruit-381-ds18b20-probe `tube`); the enclosure track sizes and checks the real groove. The ring's ID 5.94-6.20 against the 6.0 tube means at most 1 % stretch (limit < 5 %), so the squeeze comes from the groove alone. At Parker's gland depth (1.27-1.32 mm) the female groove is Ø8.54-8.64 mm: squeeze 26-29 % at nominal CS (Parker's 22-32 % over the tolerances), and the Ø9.63 OD is compressed about 10-11 % into it (Parker's own -010 groove compresses it 7.7 %). Keeping Parker's -010 groove Ø8.89 mm instead gives a 1.445 mm gland depth and 15-22 % squeeze over the CS tolerance, the low end of the compound's 15-30 %. Gland fill at depth 1.295 mm and groove width 2.42 mm is about 79 % (ring section 2.49 mm²). Throat (the bore the tube passes) clearance: Parker's .002-.005 in diametral, halved for silicone, so at most about 0.06 mm over the tube, which a printed boss holds only if reamed or printed to size.

name: AS568-010 O-ring, silicone 70A, FDA grade
part_number: S70010 (The O-Ring Store); alternate Marco S1000-010

params.note: Water 70 h at 100 °C: -2 Shore A, +3 % volume. Steam above about 250 °F (121 °C) causes reversion. High gas permeability: not for gas retention. The smart bottle's water is 0-60 °C at the probe (brief), inside this range.

params.food_contact: FDA compliant to 21 CFR 177.2600 (supplier statement for the compound)

params.note: Second source of the same size and grade: Marco Sealing Solutions S1000-010 (compound S1000, silicone 70A, orange, FDA 21 CFR 177.2600, peroxide cure, ASTM D2000 M7GE705 A19 B37 EA14 EO16 EO36 F19, -75 to 400 °F; typical hardness 68 Shore A, compression set 12 %, water 70 h at 100 °C +3 % volume). Marco states that silicones are seal materials for static applications.

Smart bottle: 1 per cap, the rod seal on the probe's Ø6 mm stainless tube in the cap floor's probe boss (brief system.md, Probe interface). Only the stainless tube passes the seal into the bottle; the PVC cable stays in the sealed compartment (brief OQ-B5). The dash size is the brief's proposal for the enclosure track.

params.resolution: The narrower -59 °C from the product page of the SKU recorded as part_number is used; it is inside the compound sheet's range. The bottle's 0 °C minimum is far from either.

params.note: A standard AS568 ring has no vendor model: the O-Ring Store and Marco product pages, the compound sheets and the Parker and Apple Rubber charts link no CAD. Generated body: library/cad/py/catalog/as568-010-silicone.py, a nominal torus from the AS568 size row.

params.reason: The size is from the AS568 row; the ring is drawn round and unloaded because its installed shape depends on the gland. The 45° split only names the contact zones for binding and is not a sealing fact.
params.value: Nominal free-state torus, ID 6.07, CS 1.78 (centre-line radius 3.925, section radius 0.89), axis Z, mid-plane z = 0; its surface split at 45° in section into four faces: bore (inner), outer, flank_a (+Z), flank_b (-Z)

fields: tensile strength (the compound sheet's 6.9 is flagged by the supplier as likely in hundreds of psi)
params.note: No source states the ring's mass. The SAE AS568 document is sold by SAE and was not read; its -010 row is taken from Parker's and Apple Rubber's charts.
